title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering

paragraphs.en: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Workflow-driven machine learning engineering (MLE) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback. However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments. Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes as they become available. To address these challenges, we propose a post-training method for autonomous long-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model. We design the Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation. Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome-guided supervision. Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome-based reward. Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends. On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3. Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）的应用正在从辅助科学研究和工程领域，扩展到自主开发和改进人工智能系统，推动“人工智能用于人工智能”（AI4AI）的发展，将其作为递归自我改进（RSI）的一条路径。 以工作流为驱动力的机器学习工程（MLE）系统通过复杂的协调机制管理长期实验，为实现这一目标提供了实用途径；而近期的 MLE 系统则采用了模型导向的交互方式，使模型能够自主组织实验，并根据执行反馈调整优化策略。 然而，每次实验的反馈都反映了此前的一系列决策，而一次长期的 MLE 运行往往包含许多此类成本高昂的实验。 因此，训练过程必须从漫长的交互轨迹中筛选出有用的监督信号，并在中间结果出现时及时从中学习。 为应对这些挑战，我们提出了一种用于自主长期 MLE 优化的后训练方法，并将其应用于训练 MLExpert——一个包含 350 亿参数的专家混合智能体模型。 我们设计了 Kaggle-MLE Factory，用于构建可执行的任务以及支持模型导向实验的交互框架。 分层智能体监督微调（SFT）通过结果导向的监督机制，将通用的工具使用能力和编码能力迁移到 MLE 中。 窗口化交互强化学习（WIRL）将连续实验结果之间的多轮决策视为一个执行窗口，并为其分配一个共享的基于结果的奖励。 异步收集与策略校正支持在轨迹结束前进行策略更新。 在 MLE-Bench Lite 测试中，MLExpert 将基础模型的平均奖牌率从 37.9% 提升至 72.7%，其性能已接近 Kimi-K3 和 GLM-5.3 等更大型的前沿模型。 进一步实验表明，MLExpert 在 NatureBench Lite、智能体框架优化和算法优化任务中的表现均有提升，说明其学到的优化能力能够泛化到其他任务中。

paragraphs.en: The rapid advancement of reasoning, code generation, and tool interaction in large language models (LLMs) is enabling artificial intelligence (AI) to move beyond assisting scientific research and engineering toward autonomously developing and improving AI systems. These efforts include model training, optimization of solver programs, and algorithm design, making AI for AI (AI4AI) a research direction toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). In this context, machine learning engineering (MLE) provides a concrete setting for this goal, requiring long-horizon optimization through repeated execution, feedback analysis, and revision rather than one-shot generation.
paragraphs.zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）在推理、代码生成和工具交互方面的快速进步，正使人工智能（AI）能够超越辅助科学研究和工程应用的范畴，迈向自主开发和改进 AI 系统的方向。 这些工作包括模型训练、求解器程序的优化以及算法设计，使得“AI 用于 AI”（AI4AI）成为实现递归自我改进（RSI）的一项研究方向。 在此背景下，机器学习工程（MLE）为这一目标提供了具体的实践场景，它需要通过反复执行、反馈分析和修订来实现长期优化，而非依赖一次性生成。

paragraphs.en: Most existing MLE systems [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] extend code generation into iterative optimization through search, memory, or multi-agent collaboration. As shown in Figure 1 (a), predefined workflows or search rules typically control experiment sequencing and stage transitions, while LLMs primarily generate or debug code at designated steps. These systems rely heavily on manually designed control logic to organize long-horizon experimentation.
paragraphs.zh: 大多数现有的 MLE 系统 [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] 通过搜索、记忆或多智能体协作，将代码生成扩展为迭代优化过程。 如图 1 (a) 所示，预定义的工作流或搜索规则通常控制实验的顺序和阶段转换，而 LLM 主要在指定步骤中生成或调试代码。 这些系统严重依赖人工设计的控制逻辑来组织长期实验。

sents.en: These systems rely heavily on manually designed control logic to organize long-horizon experimentation.

paragraphs.en: Recently, Arbor [ 4 ] and Argus [ 5 ] maintain persistent research states and allow models to design, continue, and revise experiments, placing greater demands on the model’s ability to plan experiments and sustain optimization over long interaction horizons. ML-Agent [ 6 ] combines multi-turn demonstrations with single-step RL, while Frontis-MA1 [ 7 ] trains program evolution operators through SFT and RL and integrates them into an external evolutionary search framework. These approaches primarily train models for single-step decisions or local operations within externally organized processes. In contrast, we study how to train models to organize experiments and improve solutions over sustained interaction, using experience and execution feedback from real-world MLE tasks. However, training this long-horizon optimization capability poses three challenges. 1) Open-ended MLE requires an interaction environment that preserves experimental states while leaving action selection to the model. 2) High-quality long-horizon supervision is difficult to obtain because MLE tasks are heterogeneous and interaction trajectories may mix useful exploration and failure recovery with degraded decisions. 3) Each costly experiment returns feedback on several preceding decisions before the full run ends; online RL must use this intermediate signal while handling policy mismatch during asynchronous collection.
paragraphs.zh: 最近，Arbor [ 4 ] 和 Argus [ 5 ] 保持了持续的研究状态，并允许模型设计、继续和修改实验，这对模型规划实验以及在长期交互过程中维持优化的能力提出了更高要求。 ML-Agent [ 6 ] 将多轮演示与单步强化学习相结合，而 Frontis-MA1 [ 7 ] 则通过 SFT 和 RL 训练程序演化算子，并将其整合到外部演化搜索框架中。 这些方法主要训练模型进行单步决策或执行在外部组织流程中的局部操作。 相比之下，我们研究如何训练模型来组织实验并在持续交互中改进解决方案，同时利用真实世界 MLE 任务中的经验和执行反馈。 然而，训练这种长期优化能力面临三个挑战。1) 开放式的 MLE 需要一个能够保留实验状态同时将动作选择留给模型的交互环境。2) 高质量的长期监督难以获得，因为 MLE 任务是异构的，交互轨迹可能将有益的探索和失败恢复与质量下降的决策混合在一起。3) 每次代价高昂的实验在完整运行结束前都会对之前的多个决策提供反馈；在线强化学习必须利用这种中间信号，同时处理异步收集过程中出现的策略不匹配问题。

paragraphs.en: To address these challenges, we propose a post-training method for autonomous MLE that combines a model-directed long-horizon interaction harness, hierarchical agentic SFT, and Windowed Interaction Reinforcement Learning (WIRL). Based on this, we train MLExpert , a 35B Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) agentic model, to learn long-horizon optimization strategies. As shown in Figure 1 (b), MLExpert uses sustained tool interaction within the interaction harness to autonomously organize experiments, revise solutions based on execution feedback, and maintain submission candidates. To use this intermediate feedback, WIRL treats each completed experiment as the boundary of an execution window containing decisions since the previous result. sents.en: WIRL links execution feedback to multi-turn decisions within execution windows and combines local progress rewards with policy correction for asynchronous online learning.
sents.zh: WIRL 将执行反馈与执行窗口内的多轮决策相连接，并将局部进展奖励与策略修正相结合，以实现异步在线学习。

paragraphs.en: We build the Kaggle-MLE Factory and an Interaction Harness to provide executable tasks and model-directed long-horizon interaction for training and evaluation.
paragraphs.zh: 我们构建了 Kaggle-MLE 工厂和一个交互框架，以提供可执行的任务和由模型引导的长期交互，用于训练和评估。

paragraphs.en: Extensive experiments show that MLExpert improves the base model’s average medal rate from 37.9% to 72.7% on MLE-Bench Lite, improves performance on NatureBench Lite, and generalizes to agent scaffold and algorithm optimization tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 大量实验表明，MLExpert 在 MLE-Bench Lite 上将基础模型的平均奖牌率从 37.9% 提升至 72.7%，提升了 NatureBench Lite 上的性能，并能够泛化到智能体框架和算法优化任务中。

paragraphs.en: As shown in Figure 2 , we build the Kaggle-MLE Factory to provide executable tasks and the Interaction Harness to support model-directed long-horizon experimentation and state management, together enabling hierarchical agentic SFT and WIRL for post-training MLExpert in autonomous MLE.
paragraphs.zh: 如图 2 所示，我们构建了 Kaggle-MLE Factory 以提供可执行的任务，并开发了 Interaction Harness 以支持模型引导的长期实验和状态管理。二者共同实现了分层智能体 SFT 和 WIRL，从而为自主 MLE 中的训练后 MLExpert 提供支持。

paragraphs.en: Long-horizon Agentic MLE training requires executable tasks covering diverse data modalities, objectives, and domains. Historical Kaggle competitions provide a rich source of real-world MLE problems, but their heterogeneous data organization, submission formats, and evaluation protocols make manual task adaptation difficult to scale. Therefore, we build the Kaggle-MLE Factory, which converts historical competitions into executable tasks with a public workspace, a hidden test split, and a unified evaluation interface. The Factory uses a multi-agent pipeline for task construction, validation, and repair. The discovery agent filters competitions by status, scale, and submission format. After competition data, leaderboard information, and official descriptions are collected, the analyzer agent extracts data structures, fields, and modality characteristics to form a task specification. The generator agent then prepares task data, constructs a held-out test split with hidden labels from the original labeled data, and implements the task-specific evaluator. The task is executed on real data and iteratively repaired based on validator checks of data integrity, submission format, and evaluation behavior to produce valid executable tasks. Standardized task packages support different MLE agent frameworks. Final manual review excludes tasks with unresolved label or scoring issues before trajectory collection. Appendix A details agent responsibilities and implementation.
paragraphs.zh: 长期智能体最大似然估计（MLE）训练需要涵盖多样化数据模态、目标和领域的可执行任务。 历史 Kaggle 竞赛提供了丰富的真实世界 MLE 问题，但其异构的数据组织方式、提交格式和评估协议使得手动调整任务难以规模化实施。 因此，我们构建了 Kaggle-MLE 工厂，它能够将历史竞赛转化为可执行任务，并配备公共工作区、隐藏测试集以及统一的评估接口。 该工厂采用多智能体流程进行任务构建、验证和修复。 发现智能体根据状态、规模和提交格式筛选竞赛。 在收集竞赛数据、排行榜信息和官方描述后，分析智能体会提取数据结构、字段和模态特征，形成任务规范。 随后，生成智能体准备任务数据，从原始带标签数据中构建带有隐藏标签的独立测试集，并实现任务特定的评估器。 该任务将在真实数据上执行，并根据验证器对数据完整性、提交格式和评估行为的检查进行迭代修复，以生成有效的可执行任务。 标准化的任务包支持不同的 MLE 智能体框架。 最终的人工审查会排除存在未解决的标签或评分问题的任务，然后再收集轨迹数据。 附录 A 详细说明了各智能体的职责与实现方式。

paragraphs.en: To support model-directed long-horizon MLE optimization, we design an interaction harness that follows ReAct-style loop [ 9 ] , leaving branch selection and optimization-path decisions to the model rather than an external search policy. The harness stores experimental states in solution nodes, each containing candidate code, execution logs, and metadata. Parent-linked revisions form an experiment tree that the model can revisit and compare to decide whether to continue, backtrack, or change optimization direction. The harness provides tools for solution analysis, code revision, experiment execution, history retrieval, and submission management. The model launches candidate execution through execute_code and updates its submission candidate through update_answer . The complete tool list and descriptions are provided in Appendix B .
paragraphs.zh: 为支持模型引导的长期 MLE 优化，我们设计了一种遵循 ReAct 风格循环 [9] 的交互框架，将分支选择和优化路径决策交由模型处理，而非外部搜索策略。 该框架将实验状态存储在解决方案节点中，每个节点包含候选代码、执行日志和元数据。 与父节点关联的修订版本构成一棵实验树，模型可以回溯并比较这些版本，以决定是继续执行、回退还是改变优化方向。 该框架提供了解决方案分析、代码修订、实验执行、历史记录检索和提交管理等功能工具。 模型通过 execute_code 启动候选执行，并通过 update_answer 更新其提交候选方案。 完整的工具列表及说明见附录 B。

paragraphs.en: As interaction history approaches the context limit, earlier messages are summarized while recent interactions are retained. For complex analysis, analyze delegates task analysis, data exploration, and result diagnosis to an analysis sub-agent with independent context, returning only a summary to the main model. Since overfitting or data leakage can inflate validation scores, the model can call invalidate_node based on experimental evidence and analysis to exclude unreliable candidates. With new evidence, the model can update its submission candidate while exploring alternatives.
paragraphs.zh: 随着交互历史接近上下文限制，早期消息会被摘要化，而近期的交互则会被保留。 对于复杂分析，分析模块会将任务分析、数据探索和结果诊断委托给一个具有独立上下文的分析子智能体，仅将摘要返回给主模型。 由于过拟合或数据泄露可能导致验证分数虚高，模型可以根据实验证据和分析结果调用 invalidate_node，以排除不可靠的候选方案。 在获得新证据后，模型可以在探索替代方案的同时更新其提交候选方案。

paragraphs.en: Long-horizon MLE optimization requires general tool-use, coding skills, and domain-specific decision making. We therefore use two-stage hierarchical agentic SFT. In the first stage, coding and tool-use trajectories from diverse agentic tasks are used to learn basic tool-use and code revision capabilities. The second stage adopts teacher trajectories from MLE domain and literature-derived scientific tasks to improve algorithm design, experimental analysis, and iterative optimization.

paragraphs.en: Complementary MLE demonstrations. MLE adaptation data cover both task initialization and sustained optimization. For trajectories whose first complete solution executes successfully and reaches a quality threshold, we extract the interaction prefix from task start through the corresponding execution feedback as an initial-solution trajectory , typically covering task understanding, algorithm design, and code generation. We also use long-horizon optimization trajectories from complete interactions, covering solution construction, feedback analysis, iterative revision, and final submission selection. In addition, analysis sub-agent trajectories are adopted to train the model for independent data analysis and result diagnosis.

paragraphs.en: Outcome-guided supervision selection. Long-horizon MLE trajectories can contain effective exploration and failure recovery, but may also include misguided decisions or continued degradation after reaching a strong solution. Therefore, we use execution results of submitted solutions to select high-quality trajectories and the segments used for supervision. For trajectories that pass a quality threshold, we identify the first best-performing submission and measure the subsequent performance degradation. When the post-peak degradation exceeds a threshold, we use the first best-performing submission as the anchor for retaining a trajectory prefix; otherwise, we use the last submission. The prefix ends at a complete tool-interaction boundary near the anchor. This removes degraded tails while preserving useful exploration and failure recovery before the peak.
paragraphs.zh: 以结果为导向的监督选择。 长期 MLE 轨迹可能包含有效的探索与失败恢复，但也可能包括错误的决策，或在达到优质解后持续恶化。 因此，我们利用已提交解决方案的执行结果来选择高质量轨迹以及用于监督的片段。 对于通过质量阈值的轨迹，我们会识别出首个表现最佳的提交版本，并衡量其后续的性能下降情况。 当峰值后的性能下降超过阈值时，我们将首个表现最佳的提交版本用作保留轨迹前缀的锚点；否则，则使用最后一个提交版本。 该前缀在靠近锚点处的一个完整的工具交互边界处结束。 这样既能去除恶化的尾部部分，又能保留峰值之前有益的探索与失败恢复过程。

paragraphs.en: Supervision samples and training objective. To preserve multi-turn context dependencies, each supervision sample combines existing interaction context with a continuous sequence of subsequent model actions and environment feedback from the selected MLE interactions. When context compaction occurs, the retained history and summary form the conditioning context for subsequent samples. Training loss is applied only to newly generated reasoning, text responses, and tool-call tokens, while tool feedback and inherited interaction history are used only as conditioning context and masked out from the loss. Details of outcome-guided filtering, score normalization, and the SFT objective appear in Appendix C.1 .

paragraphs.en: Building on SFT, we further optimize the long-horizon decision policy using execution feedback from the model’s own exploration. In MLE, solution quality is available only after training and evaluation, and each result depends on multiple rounds of analysis, code revision, and tool interaction. We introduce Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL), which groups consecutive model decisions made between successive experiment results into an execution window u m u_{m} . Each window is conditioned on the accumulated interaction history and associated with the outcome of the corresponding experiment launched through the execute_code tool (Sec. 3.2 ). The first window starts from the initial task state. This allows policy updates to use feedback from completed experiments without waiting for the entire task trajectory to finish.

paragraphs.en: MLExpert achieves the highest medal rate among same-scale models and reaches the performance level of larger frontier models. paragraphs.en: RL baselines and key WIRL design choices. We compare WIRL with trajectory-level GRPO and PPO-style optimization under the same MLE environment and MLE-SFT initialization. GRPO uses group-relative advantages, whereas PPO-style optimization uses a clipped objective weighted by terminal trajectory rewards without an additional critic. We also evaluate WIRL variants that remove the trend reward or policy correction separately. As shown in Table 4 , GRPO and PPO-style optimization achieve 56.1% and 60.6%, respectively, both below the 62.1% achieved by MLE-SFT, supporting WIRL’s overall design of learning from execution-window feedback. In contrast, the two WIRL variants reach 66.7% and 65.2%, respectively, while full WIRL further improves the medal rate to 72.7%, indicating that both the local trend reward and policy correction contribute to the final improvement. Further analysis in Appendix 10 shows that asynchronous execution-window collection reduces the learner waiting fraction compared with trajectory-based GRPO.

paragraphs.en: LLM agents increasingly automate data analysis, model development, and experimental iteration, with recent work extending to autonomous AI system design and improvement [ 27 ] . AIDE [ 1 ] and MLE-STAR [ 2 ] improve candidate solutions through iterative search and refinement, while MLEvolve [ 28 ] and MARS [ 29 ] use structured tree- or graph-based search, memory, and planning to organize long-horizon experimentation. R&D-Agent [ 3 ] studies multi-role collaboration, while InternAgent [ 30 ] and FM-Agent [ 31 ] extend autonomous AI research across machine learning, algorithm optimization, and engineering tasks. Recent systems including Arbor [ 4 ] and Argus [ 5 ] maintain persistent research states and increase model control.

paragraphs.en: Recent work develops MLE capabilities by training models on interaction experience. ML-Agent [ 6 ] combines multi-turn demonstrations with single-step RL, while RL for MLE Agents [ 32 ] , MLE-RL [ 33 ] , and AceGRPO [ 34 ] study online MLE training with execution feedback, asynchronous sampling, or intermediate trajectory states. Learning to Ideate [ 35 ] trains models to generate algorithm improvement suggestions, whereas Frontis-MA1 [ 7 ] applies SFT and RL to program evolution operators and combines them through an external evolutionary framework. These approaches primarily train individual interaction steps or local components of externally organized optimization workflows. SandMLE [ 36 ] applies trajectory-wise on-policy RL in micro-scale synthetic MLE environments. We train model-directed long-horizon interaction policies on real-world MLE tasks, with WIRL using execution windows to learn multi-turn decisions from delayed execution feedback under asynchronous updates.
paragraphs.zh: 近期的研究通过让模型在交互经验上进行训练，从而提升了 MLE 能力。 ML-Agent [ 6 ] 将多轮演示与单步强化学习相结合，而 RL for MLE Agents [ 32 ]、MLE-RL [ 33 ] 和 AceGRPO [ 34 ] 则研究了结合执行反馈、异步采样或中间轨迹状态的在线 MLE 训练方法。 Learning to Ideate [ 35 ] 训练模型生成算法改进建议，而 Frontis-MA1 [ 7 ] 则将 SFT 和 RL 应用于程序演化算子，并通过外部演化框架将其结合。 这些方法主要训练单个交互步骤或外部组织优化流程中的局部组件。 SandMLE [ 36 ] 在微规模的合成 MLE 环境中应用了轨迹级的在线策略强化学习。 我们在真实世界的 MLE 任务上训练了由模型引导的长期交互策略，其中 WIRL 利用执行窗口，通过异步更新从延迟的执行反馈中学习多轮决策。

paragraphs.en: Recent research has increasingly focused on post-training agentic models for sustained interaction, complex tool use, and long-horizon decision making. SWE-Gym [ 37 ] trains coding agents using trajectories collected from executable environments, while Search-R1 [ 38 ] and WebRL [ 39 ] learn multi-turn tool use from environment feedback and outcome rewards. AgentFlow [ 40 ] directly optimizes planning policies in general multi-turn agentic interaction and uses trajectory-level outcomes to train intermediate decisions. Recent work has also explored generalist agentic models for long-horizon interaction. Agents-A1 [ 41 ] uses long-horizon knowledge-action trajectories and multi-stage training, together with multi-teacher on-policy distillation (OPD), to combine capabilities from multiple domain teachers into a unified model. paragraphs.en: In this work, we introduce MLExpert, a 35B MoE agentic model trained to autonomously conduct and improve machine learning experiments over long interaction horizons. We build an automated MLE task factory and a model-directed interaction harness, and train MLExpert with hierarchical agentic SFT and WIRL to learn from teacher demonstrations and execution feedback collected from its own exploration. Extensive experiments show that MLExpert improves over its base model on MLE-Bench Lite and achieves performance comparable to larger frontier models. Further improvements on NatureBench Lite and in agent scaffold and algorithm optimization demonstrate cross-task generalization. These results support treating long-horizon optimization decision making as a trainable model capability, providing a practical path toward autonomous machine learning engineering and scientific experimentation.
paragraphs.zh: 在这项工作中，我们提出了 MLExpert——一个 35B MoE 智能体模型，经过训练能够自主执行并改进长期交互过程中的机器学习实验。 我们构建了一个自动化的 MLE 任务工厂和一个由模型引导的交互框架，并通过分层智能体 SFT 和 WIRL 训练 MLExpert，使其能够从自身探索中收集的教师演示和执行反馈中学习。 广泛的实验表明，MLExpert 在 MLE-Bench Lite 上优于其基础模型，并实现了与更大规模前沿模型相当的性能。 在 NatureBench Lite 上的进一步改进，以及在智能体框架和算法优化方面的进展，证明了其跨任务的泛化能力。 这些结果支持将长期优化决策视为一种可训练的模型能力，为自主机器学习工程和科学实验提供了一条实用路径。

paragraphs.en: We begin with a Meta-Kaggle 1 1 1 https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/kaggle/meta-kaggle competition metadata snapshot containing 11,649 entries. Guided by the task-selection principles of MLE-bench [ 8 ] , the discovery agent considers task relevance, data availability, and the feasibility of offline evaluation. Automated initial screening uses competition completion, at least 50 participating teams, and a dataset size limit of 200 GB as default criteria, checks submission-interface compatibility, and consults an exclusion list of existing tasks. The agent further selects candidates across domains and data modalities, including vision, text, audio, tabular data, and time series. Candidates are collected and processed in multiple batches.

paragraphs.en: The downloader and scraper retrieve competition data, official descriptions, and leaderboard information. The analyzer agent extracts data structures, field information, and modality characteristics to form a task specification, which the generator agent uses to produce data-preparation and scoring code. When test labels are unavailable, the pipeline constructs a held-out split from the original labeled data and keeps its labels on the evaluation side. The executor runs generated task packages on real data, while the validator agent checks structural completeness, submission-format consistency, non-degenerate labels, train–test identifier overlap, and data availability. The validator also executes the scoring function to check that it produces a valid score. Execution and validation errors are returned to the construction agents for repair. We conduct a final human review of the 160 registered tasks, excluding six with unresolved label or scoring-implementation issues and retaining 154 tasks for subsequent trajectory collection.
paragraphs.zh: 下载器和抓取器负责获取竞赛数据、官方描述以及排行榜信息。 分析智能体提取数据结构、字段信息和模态特征，形成任务规范，生成智能体则据此编写数据准备和评分代码。 当测试标签不可用时，该流程会从原始带标签的数据中构建一个预留子集，并将该子集的标签保留在评估端。 执行器在真实数据上运行生成的任务包，同时验证智能体会检查结构完整性、提交格式一致性、非退化标签、训练-测试标识符重叠情况以及数据可用性。 验证智能体还会执行评分函数，以确认其能生成有效的分数。 执行和验证过程中出现的错误会反馈给构建智能体进行修复。 我们对已注册的 160 项任务进行了最终的人工审核，排除了 6 个存在标签或评分实现问题尚未解决的任务，保留了 154 项任务用于后续轨迹收集。

paragraphs.en: Training data sources. The first SFT stage uses general coding and tool-use trajectories from StepFun [ 22 ] , while the second stage combines MLE teacher trajectories with literature-derived scientific trajectories. The MLE tasks comprise 154 tasks constructed by the Kaggle-MLE Factory and 134 tasks selected from MLE-Dojo [ 23 ] , with competitions overlapping with MLE-Bench removed. Following the task-construction approach of NatureBench [ 12 ] , we construct scientific experimentation tasks from 164 papers published in Nature-family journals, covering biology, materials science, physics, chemistry, and medicine, among other fields. The data used in these scientific tasks do not overlap with the NatureBench evaluation set. MLE teacher trajectories are generated by GLM-5.2 [ 42 ] , while scientific experimentation trajectories are generated by GLM-5.2 and Qwen3.8-Max [ 43 ] .

paragraphs.en: We use the ten-task NatureBench Lite subset listed by Frontis-MA1 [ 7 ] , with the S and M definitions from NatureBench [ 12 ] . We follow the official NatureBench evaluation protocol, with a four-hour runtime budget per task that excludes time spent scoring submissions. Following NatureBench, we compute the normalized relative gap for each evaluation instance by subtracting the paper-reported SOTA value from the agent’s primary metric value, adjusting the sign so that improvements are positive, and dividing by the absolute SOTA value. Instances without a valid submission receive a gap of − 1 -1 . The task-level score g g is the mean gap across instances. Match-SOTA and Surpass-SOTA report the percentages of tasks with g ≥ 0 g\geq 0 and g > 0.1 g>0.1 , respectively. We report a single evaluation of MLExpert over the ten tasks, with Surpass-SOTA on five tasks and Match-SOTA on seven tasks, corresponding to 50.0% and 70.0%, respectively. DeepSeek-V4-Pro Preview and MiniMax M3 [ 17 ] results are taken from Table 2 of Frontis-MA1. Our NatureBench evaluations use NVIDIA H200 GPUs; external reference results retain their original evaluation conditions.

paragraphs.en: The outer model optimizes a Python agent scaffold that calls a fixed gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 solver. All optimizers start from the same single-query scaffold and share the task environment, tools, and evaluator. Each search has a four-hour time limit and a maximum of 1,000 interaction steps, with a context limit of 200,000 tokens and an output limit of 65,536 tokens per step. The scaffold can modify prompting, calling, verification, voting, and answer-extraction procedures, with at most ten inner-model calls per problem. Initial uses one solver call, while Majority@5 takes a majority vote over five independently sampled answers.

paragraphs.en: Development uses all 30 problems from AIME 2025, with three evaluations per problem for each candidate scaffold. The outer model receives aggregate accuracy, call counts, and sanitized error summaries. Exact-request response caching is used during development to reuse inner-solver responses to identical requests. After search, the selected scaffold is frozen and evaluated using fresh solver calls on AIME 2023, 2024, and 2026. Each held-out year contains 30 problems and is evaluated three times; these years provide no feedback for scaffold development or selection. Thus, each optimizer contributes one frozen scaffold, with three evaluation repetitions per year.

paragraphs.en: Solver-call efficiency after SFT. The scaffold optimized by MLExpert-SFT achieves 38.1% held-out accuracy with 3.51 solver calls per problem, approaching the 40.0% achieved by Kimi-K3 with approximately 59% fewer calls. It also outperforms Majority@5, which reaches 24.8% with five calls per problem. MLExpert-SFT therefore improves held-out accuracy over fixed majority voting while using fewer solver calls, suggesting that its optimized scaffold uses the solver more effectively. These results indicate that SFT already supports effective scaffold optimization across held-out years.
paragraphs.zh: SFT 后的求解器调用效率。 由 MLExpert-SFT 优化的框架在测试集上实现了 38.1% 的准确率，每道题平均调用 3.51 次求解器，接近 Kimi-K3 实现的 40.0% 准确率，且调用次数减少了约 59%。 它还优于 Majority@5，后者在每道题调用五次时仅能达到 24.8% 的准确率。 因此，MLExpert-SFT 在减少求解器调用的同时，提升了测试集上的准确率，这表明其优化的框架能更有效地利用求解器。 这些结果表明，SFT 已经支持跨测试年份的有效框架优化。

paragraphs.en: Further gains from WIRL. WIRL raises held-out accuracy from 38.1% to 43.7%, a gain of 5.6 percentage points, with improvements on all three held-out years. The resulting scaffold uses 8.40 calls per problem, compared with 3.51 for MLExpert-SFT and 8.65 for Kimi-K3. With a similar number of calls to Kimi-K3, MLExpert exceeds its 40.0% accuracy, while GLM-5.3 achieves 48.1% with 9.39 calls. The SFT and RL results therefore offer different accuracy–call trade-offs: SFT yields an effective scaffold with fewer calls, while further RL finds a more accurate scaffold that uses more calls.

paragraphs.en: We evaluate 12 selected tasks spanning 12 domains in MLS-Bench-Lite. Table 12 lists the complete task set and the normalized rewards for Base and MLExpert. Both models use the same Agentic MLE harness, task descriptions, interaction tools, and official Harbor task environments.
